record.context_brief: Finite-dimensional models as submanifolds of infinite-dimensional manifolds
record.original_question: Can finite-dimensional statistical models on infinite sample spaces be profitably treated as submanifolds of an infinite-dimensional manifold so that probabilistic or statistical arguments about those models become easier to understand or simplify?

evidence.quote: It may be worth investigating whether treating such models as submanifolds of the infinite-dimensional manifold can help us understand or simplify statistical discussions about them.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(\Omega,\mathcal{F})$ be a measurable sample space (typically infinite, e.g. $\Omega=\mathbb{R}^n$ with the Borel $\sigma$-algebra) and let $\mathcal{P}(\Omega)$ denote a suitable space of probability measures on $\Omega$ that admits the structure of an infinite-dimensional Banach (or Fréchet) manifold in the sense of information geometry — for instance the Pistone–Sempi exponential statistical manifold, where $\mathcal{P}_\mu = \{p\,\mu : p>0,\ \int p\,d\mu=1\}$ is modeled on Orlicz spaces with the Young function $\Phi(x)=\cosh(x)-1$, equipped with the Fisher–Rao metric and the dual exponential/mixture connections $\nabla^{(e)}, \nabla^{(m)}$.

A finite-dimensional statistical model is a smooth injective immersion $\iota: \Theta \hookrightarrow \mathcal{P}(\Omega)$ from an open set $\Theta\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, so that $\iota(\Theta)$ is a $d$-dimensional submanifold of $\mathcal{P}(\Omega)$.

Problem. Develop a framework in which finite-dimensional statistical models on infinite sample spaces are systematically studied as submanifolds of such an infinite-dimensional manifold $\mathcal{P}(\Omega)$, and determine whether this viewpoint yields genuine simplifications or new insights for probabilistic and statistical questions about those models. Concretely: 

(a) Identify natural geometric invariants of the embedding $\iota(\Theta)\subset\mathcal{P}(\Omega)$ — such as the second fundamental form with respect to $\nabla^{(e)}$ and $\nabla^{(m)}$, the normal bundle, and curvature of the ambient manifold restricted to $\iota(\Theta)$ — and relate them to classical statistical quantities (efficiency, information loss, robustness, asymptotic expansions of estimators).

(b) Show whether projection operators (e.g. $m$- or $e$-projections from $\mathcal{P}(\Omega)$ onto $\iota(\Theta)$) provide a unified treatment of maximum likelihood estimation, model misspecification, and the EM algorithm that is strictly more transparent than purely finite-dimensional parametric arguments.

(c) Exhibit at least one concrete probabilistic or statistical statement about a finite-dimensional model on an infinite sample space whose proof is materially simplified, or whose conclusion is strengthened, by viewing the model as a submanifold of $\mathcal{P}(\Omega)$ rather than as an abstract finite-dimensional Riemannian manifold.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as a programmatic research suggestion rather than a precise conjecture. Infinite-dimensional information geometry (Pistone–Sempi exponential manifold and successors) provides partial frameworks, and there are scattered results treating parametric models as submanifolds, but no comprehensive answer establishing that this viewpoint systematically simplifies statistical arguments. We treat it as open.

status_evidence.title: An Infinite-Dimensional Geometric Structure on the Space of All the Probability Measures Equivalent to a Given One
status_evidence.snippet: Pistone and Sempi construct a Banach manifold structure on the set of probability measures equivalent to a reference measure, using Orlicz spaces.
status_evidence.claim: An infinite-dimensional manifold of probability measures exists, providing the ambient space envisioned in the problem.

status_evidence.title: Methods of Information Geometry (Amari–Nagaoka)
status_evidence.snippet: Standard reference treating finite-dimensional statistical models as Riemannian manifolds with dual connections; infinite-dimensional embedding is mentioned but not systematically developed.
status_evidence.claim: Standard treatments leave the systematic submanifold-of-infinite-dimensional-manifold viewpoint underdeveloped.
